name: Per Drop More Crop (PM-KSY)
department: Government of India / State Agri Dept
benefit: 50% to 80% Subsidy on Drip & Sprinkler Irrigation Equipment
description: Financial assistance for installing micro-irrigation systems (drip and sprinkler) to maximize water use efficiency.
benefits: Upto 80% financial subsidy for small and marginal farmers
Reduces farm water usage by up to 50%
Direct benefit transfer to vendor or farmer bank account
steps: Visit your district Agriculture/Horticulture department office
Submit land ownership records (7/12 extract) and Aadhaar card
Choose an empanelled drip irrigation manufacturer for installation

name: Soil Health Card Scheme
benefit: Free Soil Testing & Customized Fertilizer Dosage Card
description: Provides farmers with a physical Soil Health Card detailing N, P, K, micro-nutrients, and organic carbon levels every 2 years.
benefits: Free comprehensive lab test of soil samples from your land
Exact dosage recommendations for fertilizers to prevent over-use
Helps reduce fertilizer expenses by 15-20%
steps: Contact your local Gram Panchayat or Agricultural Extension Officer (AEO)
Soil samples are collected directly from your field by testing officers
Receive your Soil Health Card with recommended nutrient doses

name: Agricultural Mechanization Scheme (SMAM)
benefit: 50% to 80% Subsidy on Stubble Management Machinery
description: Promotes in-situ residue management machines like Happy Seeder, Super Seeder, Straw Chopper, and Mulchers to avoid stubble burning.
benefits: 50% subsidy for individual farmers buying Happy Seeders or Mulchers
80% financial assistance for Custom Hiring Centers (CHCs) formed by farmer groups
Allows direct seeding without removing or burning crop straw
steps: Select required machinery and submit bank details and land documents

target: High Pumping Fuel Costs & Grid Dependence
name: PM-KUSUM Solar Pump Scheme
benefit: 60% Central & State Subsidy for Off-Grid Solar Water Pumps
description: Enables farmers to install standalone solar agriculture pumps, reducing diesel fuel costs and ensuring daytime irrigation access.
benefits: 30% Central Financial Assistance + 30% State Subsidy (Total 60%)
30% bank loan facility available (farmer pays only 10% upfront)
Provides reliable daytime power for irrigation
steps: Apply online through your state Renewable Energy Development Agency portal
Provide land records, electricity connection status, and identity proof
Solar pump installed by authorized green-energy vendors

name: PM Fasal Bima Yojana (Crop Insurance)
description: Comprehensive risk insurance covering crop losses due to drought, floods, unseasonal rainfall, and pest attacks.
benefits: Nominal premium: 1.5% for Rabi crops, 2.0% for Kharif crops
Government covers up to 90% of the actuarial premium cost
Direct compensation for yield loss caused by natural calamities
steps: Enroll through your bank branch, CSC center, or PMFBY portal
Submit crop sowing certificate and land details before cutoff date

target: High Initial Cost for Sustainable Farming
name: NABARD Organic & Sustainable Credit Scheme
description: Provides low-interest credit and capital investment subsidies for setting up vermicompost units, bio-fertilizer production, and organic farming.
benefits: 25% to 33% capital subsidy on commercial bio-fertilizer and compost units
Concessional interest rate for sustainable farming group loans
Support for organic certification expenses
steps: Approach your local Cooperative Bank or Regional Rural Bank (RRB)
Submit a simple farm project plan for vermicompost or organic conversion
Bank sanctions loan with embedded NABARD capital subsidy

name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
benefit: Rs 50,000 per Hectare Assistance for Organic Clusters
description: Encourages organic cluster farming and Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) certification among smallholder farmer groups.
benefits: Rs 31,000 per hectare directly provided for organic inputs (seeds, bio-manures)
Rs 8,800 per hectare for post-harvest packaging and organic branding
Free organic certification for farmer groups
steps: Form a cluster of 20 or more farmers with a total of 50 acres
Register cluster with your local District Agriculture Extension Officer
